name: Kodo Horn
summary: In the Barrens, Kodo Horns are gathered from the roaming kodos. Tonga Runetotem uses them in herbal remedies for poisoned wildlife.

sections.title: A Reagent of the Plains
sections.body: Across the Barrens, Tonga Runetotem uses intact kodo horns in his herbal remedies. He works from the Crossroads, where the horns help strengthen his salves. Chips and fragments lack the strength he needs, so he gathers whole horns from mature kodos wandering the plains.

faq.q: What are Kodo Horns used for?
faq.answer: Tonga Runetotem uses Kodo Horns with Earthroot and pure water to brew a salve for poisoned gazelles across the Barrens. Making the remedy is part of a druid's training in natural cures for poison.
You can gather them from Barrens Kodos and Lost Barrens Kodos in the northern Barrens, between the Crossroads and the surrounding scrubland.

faq.q: Why can't druids use horn fragments instead?
faq.answer: Tonga Runetotem says chips and fragments lack the potency to balance the salve. He needs intact horns to make a remedy strong enough to counter virulent toxins.

faq.q: Is hunting kodos considered respectful for a druid?
faq.answer: Yes. Druids hunt kodos when it serves nature's balance, taking what they need to heal larger blights, such as the mysterious poisoning afflicting the native gazelle herds.

angles.text: As a Horde druid, you gather horns under Tonga Runetotem's guidance as you learn to master nature's poisons.
As a tauren, you hold kodos in high reverence and take from them with care and purpose, here to safeguard the Barrens' delicate ecosystem.
